reason: All opcodes NMOS/65SC12 (LDX zp, BNE, LDY #, JMP abs, RTS). Block is 10 bytes old and new (2+2+2+3+1 vs 3+1+2+2+2), so edge_left_loop (&1991) and all later code stay put. Shipping listing: new JMP &1987, RTS &198A, entry &198B, BNE at &198D back -8 to &1987 same page (3 taken), LDY at &198F falls into edge_left_loop &1991. Left: old LDY2+LDX3+BEQ taken same page 3 = 8, new LDX3+BNE 2+LDY2 = 7. Right: old 2+3+2+3 = 10, new 3+3+3 = 9. Saves 1 on both. edge_leave_a1 moves &1990->&198A, BNEs at &19BE/&19CB still same page; checked every build variant listing (gameplay label &197E/&198A, sky_tint &1999, sky_tint2 &19C5): the new RTS stays in the same page as the old one in each, and the back-branch to the JMP never crosses. Left entry state: Y=0, X=0, C untouched (ground_square's CLC holds), N/Z come from loads whose results do not matter, and LDA sets them first anyway. Right: edge_right (scroll_hazel.6502) starts LDA edge_x_low and writes Y (LDY #n or LDY #&21) before any read on every path; X is reloaded by calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge. Nothing falls into the inserted JMP (it follows BRA to_next_row). Callers only JSR the label; no label+offset or SMC stores into this block. tools/passcost.mjs uses the label only as a phase boundary (it still marks the entry).
